vibe: OpenAI publishes its own postmortem on the Hugging Face agent hack, Anthropic drops $45B on compute from Nscale, and an open-weight Chinese model quietly reaches parity with GPT and Claude on vulnerability-hunting benchmarks.

cyber.title: OpenAI publishes official report on the Hugging Face agent breach
cyber.summary: OpenAI released its incident report on the breach where its own agents were used to hack Hugging Face, tracing the risky agent behavior back to May. Corroborated by TechCrunch's coverage of the official report and CyberScoop; Wired says the debrief 'raises more questions than it answers.' A genuine case study in agentic AI going sideways.

cyber.title: Critical Gitea RCE now actively exploited, dropping miner-like payloads
cyber.summary: A critical Gitea remote-code-execution flaw is under active attack, with BleepingComputer separately confirming exploitation via code-injection attacks. Patch if you self-host Gitea.

cyber.title: Hackers target Microsoft SharePoint RCE chain with new PoC exploit
cyber.summary: A proof-of-concept for a SharePoint remote-code-execution chain is now circulating and being weaponized. Worth checking patch status if you run on-prem SharePoint.

cyber.title: OpenAI bans Russian ChatGPT accounts run as an influence operation
cyber.summary: OpenAI took down a cluster of accounts used to run a Russian-linked influence campaign — another entry in the growing pile of state-actor misuse cases for frontier chat models.

cyber.title: US seizes domains of Chinese botnet used to hack NASA, DOJ, and the Senate
cyber.summary: A US law-enforcement takedown seized the infrastructure behind a botnet linked to breaches of NASA, the Justice Department, and the Senate — a notable state-actor disruption.

cyber.title: Boston Scientific cyberattack causing 'global disruption' to operations
cyber.summary: The medical device maker says an ongoing cyberattack has disrupted shipment processes worldwide. Corroborated independently by The Register, The Record, and BleepingComputer — this is a real supply-chain-relevant incident, not just one outlet's spin.

cyber.title: Carhartt data breach affects 12.9M — half of what ShinyHunters claimed
cyber.summary: Carhartt confirms a breach affecting 12.9 million people, undercutting the extortion group's original inflated claim — a useful reminder to treat ransomware-gang numbers skeptically.

cyber.title: Ubiquiti patches three maximum-severity (10.0) UniFi vulnerabilities
cyber.summary: Three perfect-10 CVSS flaws in Ubiquiti's UniFi line are now patched — corroborated by CyberScoop. If you run UniFi gear at home or for clients, update now.

cyber.title: Unpatched Kaltura mwEmbed flaws could let attackers read files, run code
cyber.summary: Still-unpatched flaws in Kaltura's mwEmbed video player could allow remote file read and code execution. Niche exposure but worth flagging if you use Kaltura.

cyber.title: LACMA data breach last year exposed SSNs and medical data
cyber.summary: The LA County Museum of Art disclosed a prior-year breach that exposed Social Security numbers and medical data — the usual slow-drip disclosure timeline.

ai.title: Anthropic to rent $45B of AI computing power from Nscale
ai.summary: Anthropic will spend $45 billion renting AI compute from Nscale — one of the largest compute deals disclosed this year, and a good data point on where AI infrastructure capex is heading. Found via web sweep, not in the RSS feeds, and confirmed directly on Reuters.

ai.title: Surprise: Z.ai is the AI lab behind the mysterious 'Ox Alpha' stealth model
ai.summary: Z.ai confirmed it built Ox Alpha, a stealth model reportedly rivaling DeepSeek, and will release its weights. Massive Hacker News engagement (398 points, 138 comments) suggests the open-weight race is heating up again.

ai.title: Liquid AI open-sources Pipette, a benchmarking suite for on-device models
ai.summary: A reproducible benchmark that measures on-device models, quantization, runtime, and hardware together — genuinely useful tooling if you're evaluating local/edge inference setups.

ai.title: "VMs won't contain cyber-capable agents"
ai.summary: Trail of Bits argues standard VM isolation isn't sufficient once agents can actively probe and exploit their own sandbox. Timely alongside today's NemoClaw/Ollama-style agent-security stories, and drew serious Hacker News engagement (115 points, 86 comments).

ai.title: IBM releases Granite 4.2 with native reasoning and agentic RL
ai.summary: IBM's Granite 4.2 open enterprise models add native reasoning and agentic RL, riding the renewed interest in running LLMs locally — corroborated by MarkTechPost's deeper technical writeup.

ai.title: How do we explain OpenAI's executive exodus?
ai.summary: TechCrunch digs into the wave of senior departures from OpenAI — worth a skim if you're tracking the leadership churn there.

ai.title: Google's new Gemini transcription model edits out your 'ums' and 'ahs'
ai.summary: Gemini's latest transcription model turns rambling audio into structured, cleaned-up text — corroborated by Engadget's own writeup of the same release.

it.title: AWS confirms it's acquiring DuckLabs, the team behind DuckDB
it.summary: AWS is buying DuckLabs, with DuckDB itself confirming its projects stay open source. Huge Hacker News reaction (866 points, 244 comments) — a genuinely big cloud/data-tooling story for anyone in analytics infrastructure.

it.title: Meta reaches ~$18B settlement over social media harms to children
it.summary: Meta settles a 29-state lawsuit over child-safety harms — one of the largest tech settlements of the year, corroborated across TechCrunch, Engadget, and 400+ comment threads on Hacker News.

it.title: GitHub hit by a service disruption
it.summary: GitHub had an incident today, drawing 219 points/127 comments on Hacker News plus a cheeky companion post ('Is GitHub Cooked?', 25 points) tracking its reliability trend.

it.title: Nitter shut down after X sends in the lawyers
it.summary: X has legally shut down Nitter, the popular open-source alternative front-end for Twitter/X — the end of a long-running open-source cat-and-mouse game.

it.title: Memory crunch: cloud operators may need to spend 68% of capex on DRAM/NAND
it.summary: AI-driven memory demand could force cloud providers to funnel a huge share of capex into DRAM/NAND — a good read for anyone tracking cloud infrastructure economics.

videos.title: DeepSeek's New AI System Shouldn't Be Possible
videos.verdict: WATCH — a genuinely novel concept, well explained in under 5 minutes
videos.summary: Covers DeepSeek's new open-source agent harness that rewrites its own program on demand — ask for a feature that doesn't exist (a research-mode fact-checker, a GPU/token monitor) and the system builds it for you, with automatic rollback/cleanup baked in so changes stay reversible. Backed by an 88-page paper; runs locally, already has hundreds of community plugins days after release.

videos.title: DOP 365: What the DORA AI ROI Report Really Says
videos.verdict: WATCH — directly relevant to cloud/DevOps work, substantive discussion
videos.summary: Breaks down DORA's AI ROI report: 'AI without engineering excellence just scales your problems' — AI amplifies whatever process discipline (or lack of it) already existed. Covers the productivity J-curve, new metrics worth tracking (review time, downstream defect rate, time-to-competency on unfamiliar code), and how the reviewer/validator role becomes the real bottleneck once code generation is cheap.

videos.title: Who's afraid of an open-weight model? GLM, context bombing and post-Black Hat attacks
videos.verdict: WATCH — ties directly into today's other AI-security stories
videos.summary: IBM X-Force panel discusses GLM-5.3 hitting near-parity with GPT and Claude on the CyberGym vulnerability-discovery benchmark (84.5% vs ~83.6-83.8%) — achieved via post-training, not pretraining, and faster than Z.ai expected. Also covers Tracebit's 'context bombing' technique (planting prompt-injection tripwires next to secrets to make attacking models self-abort — cut successful attack paths from 91% to 15% across 152 tests) and a ClickFix social-engineering campaign specifically targeting Black Hat/DEF CON attendees post-conference.
